questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the initial adult lidocaine dose for medical cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is loaded at 1 - 1.5 mg/kg in medical cardiac arrest; 0.75 mg/kg is the repeat bolus, 3 mg/kg the cumulative ceiling, and 4 mg/kg the local-anesthesia maximum.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the maximum amount of lidocaine permitted for an adult in medical cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: Cardiac arrest dosing stops at 3 doses or 3 mg/kg, whichever comes first. 4 mg/kg is the separate ceiling for local infiltration and 40 mg is the IO pain dose.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: A patient achieves ROSC after a lidocaine bolus during resuscitation. What is the adult lidocaine infusion rate for post-ROSC management?
questions.explanation: The post-ROSC maintenance infusion is 1 - 4 mg/min, and it is only started if ROSC followed a bolus dose given during the resuscitation.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the adult lidocaine repeat dose and interval when treating tachycardias?
questions.explanation: Tachycardia repeat dosing is 0.5 - 0.75 mg/kg every 3 - 5 minutes, which is faster and lower than the cardiac arrest repeat of 0.75 mg/kg every 5 - 10 minutes. Both cap at 3 doses or 3 mg/kg.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the maximum lidocaine dose for local anesthesia at an adult chest tube site?
questions.explanation: Up to 5 mL of 2% lidocaine is fanned out across the insertion area, not to exceed 4 mg/kg. The 3 mg/kg ceiling belongs to the antiarrhythmic indications.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: For a child under 25 kg, what is the maximum lidocaine dose for local anesthesia at a chest tube site?
questions.explanation: Children over 25 kg follow the adult 4 mg/kg limit, but under 25 kg the limit is expressed by volume: 0.2 mL/kg of the 2% solution.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the adult lidocaine dose for intraosseous infusion pain management?
questions.explanation: 40 mg is pushed slowly over 120 seconds and allowed to dwell in the marrow space for 60 seconds before flushing, which is what actually produces the analgesia.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: What is the lidocaine dose for intraosseous infusion pain management in a child weighing less than 20 kg?
questions.explanation: Children at or above 20 kg get the adult 40 mg; below 20 kg the dose is 0.5 mg/kg, still given over 120 seconds with a 60 second dwell and capped at 40 mg.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: Into which pharmacologic category does the formulary place lidocaine?
options: Antiarrhythmic Agent, Class Ib; Local Anesthetic
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is a Class Ib antiarrhythmic that also works as a local anesthetic, which is why the same drug appears for both cardiac arrest and chest tube infiltration.

questions.title: Lidocaine
questions.stem: Which rhythm is listed as a contraindication to lidocaine?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is contraindicated in supraventricular dysrhythmias and heart block, along with hypersensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics; the ventricular indications are exactly where it is used.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: What is the adult loading dose of lipid emulsion 2% for beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose?
questions.explanation: The rescue bolus is 1.5 mL/kg pushed over 1 minute; giving it slowly defeats the purpose, as the goal is a rapid lipid load to bind circulating drug.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: After the lipid emulsion bolus for beta blocker overdose, at what rate is the infusion run?
questions.explanation: The bolus is followed immediately by a 0.25 - 0.5 mL/kg/min infusion to maintain the lipid compartment; 1.5 mL/kg is the bolus, not an infusion rate.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: Lipid emulsion 2% is carried on the LFN formulary for which toxicologic emergency?
options: Beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose
questions.explanation: The only standing-order indication is beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose. Acetaminophen overdose is treated with N-acetylcysteine and clonidine or opioid overdose with naloxone.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: What is the leading theorized mechanism by which lipid emulsion reverses a lipophilic drug overdose?
options: It inhibits cAMP phosphodiesterase in cardiac muscle
It acts as a lipid sink, surrounding the lipophilic drug molecule
It competitively displaces the drug from its receptor
It blocks calcium ion influx into vascular smooth muscle
questions.explanation: The lipid sink theory holds that the emulsion sequesters the lipophilic drug and renders it ineffective; a second theory is that the fatty acids give the myocardium a ready energy source.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of lipid emulsion 2%?
questions.explanation: It is classed simply as a sterile fat emulsion, which is why its contraindications are about fat metabolism and food protein allergy rather than cardiovascular effects.

questions.title: Lipid Emulsion 2%
questions.stem: Which hypersensitivity is a contraindication to lipid emulsion 2%?
questions.explanation: The emulsion contains soy oil and egg lecithin, so hypersensitivity to egg, soy or peanut protein is a contraindication, as is any impaired ability to metabolize fat.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for a combative patient?
questions.explanation: Combative patients get 1 - 4 mg IV/IM repeated every 20 minutes. The 2 - 4 mg q 5 min regimen is the seizure dose and is deliberately more aggressive.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the pediatric lorazepam dose for a combative patient?
questions.explanation: Children are dosed at 0.05 - 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM every 20 minutes for agitation; 0.1 mg/kg q 5 min is the pediatric seizure dose and 0.05 mg/kg is for refractory nausea.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for seizures?
options: 1 - 4 mg IV, may repeat q 45 min
questions.explanation: Seizures get 2 - 4 mg IV/IM repeated as often as every 5 minutes; the 20 minute and 45 minute intervals belong to agitation and post-intubation sedation respectively.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the pediatric lorazepam dose for seizures?
options: 0.05 - 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM, may repeat q 45 min
questions.explanation: Pediatric seizures are treated with 0.1 mg/kg every 5 minutes PRN, capped at a 4 mg single dose - a higher per-kilo dose and shorter interval than the agitation regimen.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the maximum single pediatric lorazepam dose for seizures?
questions.explanation: The pediatric seizure single-dose ceiling is 4 mg. The 1 mg cap belongs to anxiolysis dosing and the 5 mg total cap to shivering after rapid cooling.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for anxiolysis?
questions.explanation: Anxiolysis uses a much smaller weight-based dose, 0.01 mg/kg every 20 minutes PRN with a 1 mg per dose ceiling, because the goal is calm rather than sedation.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the maximum single lorazepam dose when it is given for anxiolysis?
questions.explanation: Anxiolysis is capped at 1 mg per dose even if the 0.01 mg/kg calculation yields more, which keeps a large patient from being over-sedated for anxiety alone.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for refractory nausea?
questions.explanation: Refractory nausea - nausea that has not responded to a primary antiemetic - is treated with a small 0.5 - 1 mg IV/IM dose of lorazepam.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for shivering secondary to rapid cooling for heat stroke?
questions.explanation: Shivering defeats active cooling by generating heat, so 1 mg PRN is given to suppress it, to a total of 5 mg.

questions.title: Lorazepam
questions.stem: What is the adult lorazepam dose for post-intubation sedation?
options: 1 - 4 mg IV, may repeat q 45 min
questions.explanation: Post-intubation sedation is 1 - 4 mg IV repeated every 45 minutes, reflecting lorazepam's longer duration once the airway is already secured.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the adult magnesium sulfate dose for torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: Torsades gets 2 grams IV over 15 minutes. The 6 gram loads belong to the obstetric indications, and the 20 minute infusion is the asthma dose.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the pediatric magnesium sulfate dose for torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: Children in torsades get 25 - 50 mg/kg over 15 minutes, capped at 2 grams per dose; 50 mg/kg over 20 minutes is the pediatric asthma dose.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the adult magnesium sulfate dose for asthma?
questions.explanation: Magnesium for bronchospasm is 2 grams over 20 minutes; the slower infusion limits the hypotension and flushing that a faster push causes.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the pediatric magnesium sulfate dose for asthma?
questions.explanation: Pediatric asthma is treated with 50 mg/kg IV over 20 minutes, not to exceed 2 grams - the same ceiling as the adult dose.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the maximum pediatric magnesium sulfate dose per dose for torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: The weight-based pediatric dose is capped at 2 grams per dose, so a large adolescent receives no more magnesium than an adult would.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the adult magnesium sulfate regimen for pre-term labor or a prolapsed cord?
options: 2 grams IV over 15 minutes, then 2 grams/hr infusion
6 grams over 15 minutes, then 2 grams/hr infusion
6 grams over 30 minutes, then 2 grams/hr infusion
2 grams over 20 minutes, then 1 gram/hr infusion
questions.explanation: Tocolysis uses a 6 gram load over 30 minutes followed by a 2 grams/hr infusion. The eclampsia load is the same amount but delivered faster, over 15 minutes.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the adult magnesium sulfate loading dose for eclamptic seizures if magnesium has not already been given?
questions.explanation: An actively seizing eclamptic patient gets 6 grams over 15 minutes, then a 2 grams/hr infusion. The 30 minute load is for tocolysis, where there is no seizure to stop.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: An eclamptic patient already on a magnesium infusion continues to seize. What does the formulary direct?
options: Give an additional 2 grams over 2 minutes and increase the infusion by 1 gram/hr
Repeat the full 6 gram load over 15 minutes and continue the infusion
Increase the infusion to 4 grams/hr without an additional bolus
Give an additional 2 grams over 20 minutes and hold the infusion
questions.explanation: Persistent eclamptic seizures are answered with a 2 gram bolus over 2 minutes plus a 1 gram/hr step up in the infusion, rather than repeating the whole load.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: Which drug is given to treat magnesium toxicity?
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate antagonizes magnesium at the neuromuscular junction and is the antidote whenever toxicity appears during a magnesium infusion.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the therapeutic magnesium level for PIH and pre-term labor?
questions.explanation: The target serum range for pregnancy-induced hypertension and tocolysis is 4 - 7 mEq/L; levels above this band are where reflex loss and respiratory depression begin.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: Which examination finding is an early sign of magnesium toxicity?
questions.explanation: Loss of deep tendon reflexes, along with weakness, bradypnea and hypotension, signals magnesium toxicity, which is why DTRs are checked serially during an infusion.

questions.title: Magnesium Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of magnesium sulfate?
options: Antiarrhythmic Agent, Class Ib; Local Anesthetic
questions.explanation: Magnesium is listed as an antiarrhythmic, tocolytic and electrolyte, which maps onto its three uses: torsades, pre-term labor, and replacement or bronchodilation.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: What is the mannitol dose for cerebral edema due to DKA or herniation from head injury or ICH?
questions.explanation: Mannitol is given at 0.5 - 1 gram/kg over 15 minutes for cerebral edema or herniation, and the pediatric dose is the same as the adult dose.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of mannitol?
questions.explanation: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic: it draws water into the intravascular space and then forces diuresis by raising the osmotic pressure of glomerular filtrate.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: Which condition is a contraindication to mannitol?
questions.explanation: Mannitol transiently expands intravascular volume, so marked pulmonary edema or CHF contraindicates it - along with intracranial bleeding, shock and severe dehydration.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: Mannitol concentrations greater than 15% require what during administration?
questions.explanation: Concentrations above 15% crystallize readily, so an in-line IV filter is required to keep crystals from reaching the patient.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: Which product must not be co-administered with mannitol?
questions.explanation: Mannitol is not given with blood products. If both are needed, they require separate access or separate timing.

questions.title: Mannitol
questions.stem: When can a rebound increase in ICP occur after mannitol administration?
questions.explanation: Rebound ICP elevation is described about 12 hours post administration, which matters on long transports and for handoff to the receiving team.

questions.title: Methylergonovine
questions.stem: What is the adult methylergonovine dose for postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: Methylergonovine is 0.2 mg IM every 2 to 4 hours. The intramuscular route matters: routine IV administration risks a sudden hypertensive or cerebrovascular event.

questions.title: Methylergonovine
questions.stem: Methylergonovine must be withheld when the systolic blood pressure is above what value?
questions.explanation: A systolic above 140 is an outright contraindication, because the drug's vasoconstriction can push an already hypertensive postpartum patient into a cerebrovascular event.

questions.title: Methylergonovine
questions.stem: Why is methylergonovine not given by routine IV administration?
options: Risk of sudden hypertensive and cerebrovascular accidents
Risk of crystallizing in the IV line
Risk of severe hypotension and reflex tachycardia
questions.explanation: IV administration produces an abrupt pressor response; the formulary reserves it and directs the IM route for routine postpartum hemorrhage dosing.

questions.title: Methylergonovine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of methylergonovine?
questions.explanation: Methylergonovine is an ergot alkaloid, which explains both its uterotonic effect and its vasoconstrictive side effect profile.

questions.title: Methylergonovine
questions.stem: How does methylergonovine control postpartum hemorrhage?
options: It increases uterine contraction force and frequency
It promotes platelet aggregation at the placental bed
It selectively constricts the uterine arteries
It replaces fibrinogen and corrects a coagulopathy
questions.explanation: It works by increasing the force and frequency of uterine contractions, which mechanically compresses the bleeding vessels of an atonic uterus.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: What is the adult methylprednisolone dose for an allergic reaction or asthma/COPD?
questions.explanation: Adults get 125 mg IV for allergic reactions, asthma/COPD, epiglottitis and croup, and high altitude emergencies - a single flat dose regardless of indication.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: What is the pediatric methylprednisolone dose for asthma or an allergic reaction?
questions.explanation: Children are dosed at 2 mg/kg IV with a 60 mg ceiling, so even a large child receives well under the adult 125 mg dose.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: What is the maximum pediatric methylprednisolone dose?
questions.explanation: The 2 mg/kg pediatric calculation is capped at 60 mg per dose; 125 mg is the adult flat dose and would be an overdose in a child.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: Under what conditions may methylprednisolone be given for refractory hypotension in septic shock?
options: Only after an arterial line has been placed
If the patient remains hypotensive after two fluid boluses
If the patient remains hypotensive despite epinephrine
If hydrocortisone is unavailable and with a provider order
questions.explanation: Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV is a substitute for hydrocortisone in refractory septic shock; it is not a first-line steroid here and requires a provider order.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of methylprednisolone?
questions.explanation: Methylprednisolone is a glucocorticoid corticosteroid; it decreases inflammation by suppressing leukocyte migration and reversing increased capillary permeability.

questions.title: Methylprednisolone
questions.stem: Which cardiac adverse reactions does the formulary list for methylprednisolone?
questions.explanation: Bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmia, cardiomegaly and circulatory shock are listed, which is why a steroid is not a harmless add-on in an unstable patient.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: What is the adult metoprolol dose for aortic emergencies or STEMI?
options: 5 mg IV, up to two total doses
2.5 mg IV q 15 min, max 15 mg
5 mg IV, may repeat x2 q 5 min
questions.explanation: Aortic emergencies and STEMI get 5 mg IV repeated up to twice at 5 minute intervals, to a 15 mg maximum - faster and larger than the narrow complex tachycardia regimen.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: What is the adult metoprolol dose for narrow complex tachycardias?
options: 5 mg IV, may repeat x2 q 5 min
questions.explanation: Rate control of a narrow complex tachycardia uses 2.5 - 5 mg every 15 minutes to a maximum of 15 mg, allowing the heart rate response to be assessed between doses.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: What is the maximum total metoprolol dose for narrow complex tachycardias?
questions.explanation: Both the tachycardia and the aortic/STEMI regimens stop at 15 mg total, after which further beta blockade is a physician decision.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: How is metoprolol used in refractory ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest?
options: 2.5 - 5 mg IV after the third defibrillation attempt
5 mg IV, up to two total doses in place of additional epinephrine
5 mg IV given with every other dose of epinephrine
5 mg IV immediately before each defibrillation attempt
questions.explanation: In refractory v-fib, up to two 5 mg doses replace additional epinephrine rather than being added to it - the point is to reduce catecholamine-driven refractoriness.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of metoprolol?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol is a beta blocker - a selective inhibitor of beta-1 adrenergic receptors - which is why its adverse effects are bradycardia, hypotension and bronchospasm.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: Which conduction abnormality contraindicates metoprolol unless the patient has a functioning artificial pacemaker?
questions.explanation: Second- and third-degree block are contraindications because further AV nodal blockade can stop conduction entirely; a functioning pacemaker removes that risk.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: What effect may amiodarone have when it is given with metoprolol?
options: It may trigger a hypertensive crisis
It may blunt the beta blockade and shorten its duration
It may enhance the bradycardic effect, even to cardiac arrest
questions.explanation: Amiodarone can enhance beta blocker bradycardia to the point of cardiac arrest and can raise beta blocker serum concentrations, so pairing them deserves deliberate thought.

questions.title: Metoprolol
questions.stem: Beta blockers may increase the serum concentration of which drug?
questions.explanation: Beta blockers raise lidocaine levels, which matters when both are used in the same arrest. Nifedipine and nitroprusside instead have their hypotensive effects enhanced.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the adult midazolam IV/IM dose for a combative patient?
questions.explanation: Adults get 2 - 5 mg IV/IM repeatable every 15 minutes for agitation, with lower doses considered for frail, elderly or debilitated patients.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the intranasal midazolam dose for a combative patient?
questions.explanation: The IN route is 0.3 mg/kg to a 10 mg maximum for adults and children alike, split between both nostrils so the volume per nostril is actually absorbed.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the pediatric midazolam IV/IM dose for a combative patient?
questions.explanation: Children get 0.05 - 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM repeatable every 15 minutes for agitation; 0.1 mg/kg q 5 min is the seizure regimen and 0.3 mg/kg is the intranasal dose.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the adult midazolam dose for post-intubation sedation?
questions.explanation: Post-intubation sedation is 2 - 5 mg IV, capped at 5 mg per dose and repeatable every 15 minutes; an infusion should be considered for long transports.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: After the bolus, at what rate is an adult midazolam infusion started?
options: 2 mg/hr if under 100 kg, 4 mg/hr if 100 kg or more
4 mg/hr if under 100 kg, 2 mg/hr if 100 kg or more
questions.explanation: The adult infusion is banded by weight: 2 mg/hr under 100 kg and 4 mg/hr at or above 100 kg, titrated by 1 mg/hr every 5 - 10 minutes with a 2 mg bolus between titrations.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the maximum adult midazolam infusion rate?
questions.explanation: The adult infusion ceiling is 10 mg/hr; beyond that, sedation should be reconsidered rather than simply titrated higher.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: At what rate is a pediatric midazolam infusion started after the bolus?
questions.explanation: Pediatric infusions start at 50 mcg/kg/hr and are titrated by 10 mcg/kg/hr every 5 - 10 minutes, with an additional bolus given before each titration.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the maximum pediatric midazolam infusion rate?
questions.explanation: The pediatric infusion is capped at 100 mcg/kg/hr, twice the starting rate of 50 mcg/kg/hr.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the midazolam IV/IM dose for seizures?
options: 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM, max single dose 5 mg
0.01 mg/kg IV, max single dose 5 mg
questions.explanation: Seizures are treated with 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM, repeatable every 5 minutes with a 5 mg single-dose ceiling; the pediatric dose is the same as the adult dose.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the adult midazolam dose for RSI induction?
questions.explanation: Standard RSI induction is 0.2 mg/kg IV to a maximum of 20 mg; the pediatric induction dose is half that at 0.1 mg/kg.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What midazolam induction dose is used for RSI in a hypotensive adult?
questions.explanation: The induction dose is halved to 0.1 mg/kg in hypotension, because midazolam's own vasodilation and myocardial depression can collapse an already marginal blood pressure.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the maximum midazolam dose for RSI induction?
questions.explanation: RSI induction is capped at 20 mg for both adults and children. The 10 mg cap belongs to intranasal dosing and 5 mg to seizure and post-intubation dosing.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the midazolam dose for anxiolysis?
questions.explanation: Anxiolysis uses a tenth of the seizure dose - 0.01 mg/kg IV every 15 minutes PRN, max 5 mg per dose - because the intent is to take the edge off, not to sedate.

questions.title: Midazolam
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of midazolam?
questions.explanation: Midazolam is a short-acting parenteral benzodiazepine, which is why its warnings centre on alcohol intoxication and concurrent opioid use.

questions.title: Milrinone
questions.stem: What is the milrinone loading dose for pulmonary edema or CHF?
questions.explanation: Milrinone is loaded at 50 mcg/kg over 10 minutes before the infusion starts; the pediatric dose is the same as the adult dose.

questions.title: Milrinone
questions.stem: After the milrinone load, at what rate is the infusion run?
questions.explanation: The maintenance infusion is 0.375 to 0.75 mcg/kg/min. Because milrinone is both an inotrope and a vasodilator, the low end is the safer starting point in a marginal blood pressure.

questions.title: Milrinone
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of milrinone?
questions.explanation: Milrinone is an inotrope and vasodilator - it increases contractile force while reducing afterload, which is why hypotension is its signature adverse effect.

questions.title: Milrinone
questions.stem: Which adverse reactions does the formulary list for milrinone?
questions.explanation: Hypotension, ventricular arrhythmias and headache are the listed reactions; the hypotension follows directly from milrinone's vasodilating action.

questions.title: Milrinone
questions.stem: In which cardiac condition should milrinone be used with caution?
questions.explanation: Severe aortic stenosis, pulmonic valve disease and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy all call for caution, because a fixed outflow obstruction cannot compensate for the vasodilation.

questions.title: Morphine Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the adult morphine dose for pain management?
questions.explanation: Adults get 2 - 5 mg IV/IM, repeatable every 5 minutes PRN, titrated to the patient's pain and respiratory status.

questions.title: Morphine Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the pediatric morphine dose for pain management?
questions.explanation: Children get 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM with a 5 mg ceiling, repeatable every 5 minutes - the same upper bound as the adult single dose.

questions.title: Morphine Sulfate
questions.stem: Which obstetric finding is listed as a contraindication to morphine?
questions.explanation: Fetal acidosis or a non-reassuring fetal heart tracing contraindicates morphine, since opioids given in labor can further depress an already compromised fetus.

questions.title: Morphine Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of morphine sulfate?
questions.explanation: Morphine is an opioid analgesic acting on opiate receptors in the brain; it also increases peripheral venous capacitance and decreases venous return.

questions.title: Morphine Sulfate
questions.stem: What is the listed onset and duration of morphine sulfate?
questions.explanation: Morphine acts within 30 seconds and lasts 2 - 4 hours. That long tail outlives naloxone's roughly 45 minute duration, so a reversed patient can re-sedate in flight.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: What is the oral loading dose of N-acetylcysteine for acetaminophen overdose?
questions.explanation: The oral load is 140 mg/kg given by mouth or down an NG/OG tube; 150 mg/kg is the parenteral load, and the two routes must not be confused.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: After the oral N-acetylcysteine load, what additional dose is given and how often?
questions.explanation: Oral maintenance is 70 mg/kg every 4 hours for 68 hours - half the loading dose, continued well beyond the transport, so the receiving facility must be told when the load was given.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: What is the parenteral N-acetylcysteine loading dose for acetaminophen overdose?
options: 150 mg/kg in 200 mL D5W over 60 minutes
100 mg/kg in 1000 mL D5W over 16 hours
50 mg/kg in 500 mL D5W over 4 hours
140 mg/kg in 200 mL D5W over 60 minutes
questions.explanation: The IV load is 150 mg/kg in 200 mL of D5W infused over 60 minutes, and it is the first of three sequential bags.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: What is the second parenteral N-acetylcysteine infusion after the loading dose?
options: 150 mg/kg in 200 mL D5W over 60 minutes
70 mg/kg in 500 mL D5W over 4 hours
50 mg/kg in 500 mL D5W over 4 hours
100 mg/kg in 1000 mL D5W over 16 hours
questions.explanation: After the load, 50 mg/kg is mixed in 500 mL of D5W and the whole volume is infused over 4 hours - the bag a transport crew is most likely to inherit in progress.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: What is the final parenteral N-acetylcysteine infusion after the first two bags?
options: 100 mg/kg in 1000 mL D5W over 16 hours
140 mg/kg in 1000 mL D5W over 16 hours
150 mg/kg in 200 mL D5W over 60 minutes
50 mg/kg in 500 mL D5W over 4 hours
questions.explanation: The third bag is 100 mg/kg in 1000 mL of D5W over 16 hours, completing the 21 hour IV protocol.

questions.title: N-acetylcysteine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of N-acetylcysteine?
questions.explanation: N-acetylcysteine is an antidote and mucolytic; in acetaminophen overdose it replenishes glutathione, and delay in giving it increases the risk of hepatic injury.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the adult naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
questions.explanation: Opioid overdose is treated with 0.4 mg IV/IM/IN repeated every 3 - 5 minutes PRN, titrated to respiratory function rather than to full wakefulness.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the pediatric naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
questions.explanation: Children get 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM/IN, repeatable every 3 - 5 minutes PRN, with a single-dose ceiling of 0.4 mg - the adult dose.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the maximum single pediatric naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
questions.explanation: The pediatric single-dose cap for opioid overdose is 0.4 mg. The 2 mg and 10 mg limits belong to the much larger clonidine overdose dosing.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the naloxone dose for clonidine overdose in an opioid-naive adult?
options: 0.1 mg/kg IV, max 10 mg per dose
0.4 mg IV, max 2 mg per dose
0.1 mg/kg IV, max 2 mg per dose
0.5 mg IV, max 10 mg per dose
questions.explanation: Clonidine overdose needs far more naloxone than opioid overdose: 0.1 mg/kg IV, max 2 mg per dose, repeated every 1 - 2 minutes PRN to a 10 mg total.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the maximum total naloxone dose when treating clonidine overdose in an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Dosing for clonidine overdose continues every 1 - 2 minutes up to 10 mg total, which is an order of magnitude above a typical opioid reversal.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: In an opioid-dependent patient with clonidine overdose, what naloxone dose is given for respiratory depression?
questions.explanation: Opioid-dependent patients are dosed more cautiously to avoid precipitating withdrawal: 0.5 mg IV for respiratory depression, rising to 1 mg IV if the patient is apneic.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: In an opioid-dependent patient with clonidine overdose who is apneic, what naloxone dose is given?
questions.explanation: Apnea in an opioid-dependent patient justifies the larger 1 mg IV dose, repeated every 1 - 2 minutes PRN, because the airway threat outweighs the withdrawal risk.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of naloxone?
questions.explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist and antidote: it competes for and displaces narcotic molecules from opiate receptors in the brain.

questions.title: Naloxone
questions.stem: Which history is listed as a contraindication to naloxone because it may precipitate seizures?
questions.explanation: A mother or infant with a history of opioid addiction or on methadone is a listed contraindication, since abrupt reversal in that setting may precipitate seizures.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is the adult nicardipine starting infusion rate for hypertension?
questions.explanation: Nicardipine is started at 5 mg/hr; 2.5 mg/hr is the titration increment and 15 mg/hr is the maximum rate.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: How is an adult nicardipine infusion titrated?
questions.explanation: The infusion is increased by 2.5 mg/hr every 5 minutes until the target pressure is reached, then decreased as needed to hold the desired BP.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is the maximum adult nicardipine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: The adult ceiling is 15 mg/hr. Once the blood pressure goal is met the rate is decreased, not simply left at the maximum.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is the pediatric nicardipine dose for hypertension?
questions.explanation: Children are dosed at 0.5 - 1 mcg/kg/min and titrated every 15 - 30 minutes to the BP goal, a much slower titration than the adult every-5-minute schedule.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is the maximum pediatric nicardipine rate?
questions.explanation: The pediatric rate is capped at 5 mcg/kg/min, five times the upper end of the 0.5 - 1 mcg/kg/min starting range.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is required before starting nicardipine in a pediatric patient?
questions.explanation: Pediatric nicardipine is not a standing order - a physician order is required to initiate it, even though adult dosing may be started by the crew.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of nicardipine?
questions.explanation: Nicardipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker: it relaxes vascular smooth muscle with little negative inotropic effect, which is why it is the infusion of choice for hypertension.

questions.title: Nicardipine
questions.stem: Two 25 mg vials of nicardipine are injected into a 250 mL bag after 20 mL is removed. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: Fifty milligrams in the resulting 250 mL yields 0.2 mg/mL, matching the premixed 50 mg / 250 mL bag so the pump settings do not change.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: What is the adult nifedipine dose for high altitude pulmonary edema?
questions.explanation: HAPE is treated with a single 20 mg oral dose; the 10 mg repeating regimen belongs to pre-term labor and would under-dose the altitude indication.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: What is the adult nifedipine dose for pre-term labor?
questions.explanation: Tocolysis uses 10 mg PO or SL every 15 minutes to a total of 40 mg, titrated against the blood pressure rather than given as one large dose.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: What is the maximum total nifedipine dose for pre-term labor?
questions.explanation: Repeat dosing stops at 40 mg total. 20 mg is the single HAPE dose and 10 mg is each individual tocolytic dose.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: At what systolic blood pressure is nifedipine held during pre-term labor?
questions.explanation: Nifedipine is held for a systolic under 90 because its vasodilation will worsen maternal hypotension and reduce uterine perfusion.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of nifedipine?
questions.explanation: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker classed with the antianginals; it inhibits calcium influx into vascular smooth muscle and myocardium.

questions.title: Nifedipine
questions.stem: Which adverse reactions does the formulary list for nifedipine?
questions.explanation: Hypotension, arrhythmia, pulmonary edema, Stevens Johnson syndrome, nausea/vomiting and palpitations are listed - note that pulmonary edema appears as an adverse effect even though nifedipine treats HAPE.
